plain_english_question: Who funds the grid, power, and data-center buildout, and who gets paid as load becomes infrastructure?
why_it_matters: This is one of the clearest real-economy capital destinations: money has to become generation, transmission, distribution, substations, data centers, contractors, and equipment.
best_companies_or_cases: FPL/NextEra; AEP; Duke; Blackstone/Brookfield infrastructure comparison route; Sterling and MasTec as contractor beneficiaries
strongest_evidence: Utility dockets, recovery routes, category cost/recovery proxies, load/resource-plan evidence, and contractor backlog/cash-proxy evidence are visible.
missing_documents: Billing determinants, collected customer receipts, signed hyperscaler/customer contracts, project source/use, in-service status, earned-return workpapers, and project-level return model.
next_extraction: Build a power/grid/data-center customer-cash map joining utility recovery filings, customer/load obligations, contractor backlog, and equipment supplier beneficiaries.
writing_safe_claim: Power/grid and data-center demand is visible as a capital destination, and selected utility recovery routes are document-backed.
do_not_claim_yet: Data-center or AI load has already produced full project cash returns, or every utility/customer/contractor dollar is proven.

plain_english_question: How do insurance and retirement liabilities become credit assets, and what cash comes back to the legal entity?
why_it_matters: This is the cleanest way to see big platforms below the marketing layer: statutory entities disclose assets, income, credit quality, and sometimes proceeds.
best_companies_or_cases: KKR/Global Atlantic / Accordia; Apollo/Athene; Brookfield Wealth Solutions; Blackstone insurance-client channel
strongest_evidence: Accordia has a 7.318321094B USD owned-bond book, 229.507957M USD statutory interest received, same-CUSIP continuity rows, and selected disposal consideration columns.
missing_documents: Bank/custodian settlement, borrower use, liability-cost spread, reinsurance/funds-held waterfall, collateral, NAIC migration, and return model.
next_extraction: Finish Accordia disposal proof packet, then repeat the statutory Schedule D/BA income and credit-quality bridge for Apollo/Athene and other insurance entities.
writing_safe_claim: Insurance statutory filings can show legal-entity assets and cash-back proxy evidence at a much higher resolution than platform AUM claims.
do_not_claim_yet: Policyholder dollars are directly allocated to each asset, or statutory interest/proceeds columns prove full platform profit.

plain_english_question: What collateral backs the money, and does asset-level cash support the borrowing?
why_it_matters: Collateral lanes are where annual reports can expose the legal borrowing base: fleet, receivables, inventory, ABS, and securitization wrappers.
best_companies_or_cases: United Rentals; Accordia ABS/private-marker rows; Target; Zebra; Pool; MSC Industrial; Global Industrial
strongest_evidence: URI has fleet, ABL, AR securitization, liquidity, rental revenue, OCF, and capex coverage evidence; insurance statutory schedules surface ABS-style assets.
missing_documents: Populated borrowing-base certificates, eligible collateral tapes, NOLV/reserve deductions, trustee remittance reports, receivable collections, and asset-class lifecycle ROIC.
next_extraction: Build the collateral proof lane: URI borrowing-base certificate chase plus receivable/inventory extraction for selected distributors and retailers.
writing_safe_claim: Asset-backed and collateral channels are visible, but borrowing capacity must be separated from actual eligible collateral and cash conversion.
do_not_claim_yet: Reported assets or liquidity prove collateral availability, trustee cash, or asset-level return.

plain_english_question: Which private borrowers received money, what facility carried it, and what did they do with it?
why_it_matters: This is the direct answer to who is investing where, but it usually needs documents beyond ordinary annual reports.
best_companies_or_cases: Ares/Frontline; Auctane; Medallia; Atwell; selected BDC borrower schedules; BlackRock/HPS and Blackstone borrower candidates
strongest_evidence: Borrower and holder rows are visible across BDC/private-credit evidence, and Ares has the strongest named borrower route in the local stack.
missing_documents: Credit agreement, total facility size, lender allocation, closing funds-flow, borrower bank receipt, use of proceeds, collateral package, debt service, and repayment.
next_extraction: Pick one Ares/Frontline-style borrower and create a source request packet plus public credit-agreement/rating-report search log.
writing_safe_claim: Private-credit destination evidence exists at borrower/holder level; cash receipt and use remain the decisive proof gap.
do_not_claim_yet: Private credit has broadly replaced banks, or holder fair value equals borrower cash received.

plain_english_question: How does corporate cash, debt, or project finance become LNG, midstream, fleet, and construction capacity?
why_it_matters: This lane ties financing to physical output: trains, cargoes, pipelines, terminals, fleets, backlog, and construction execution.
best_companies_or_cases: Cheniere; Energy Transfer; ONEOK; Targa; United Rentals; Sterling
strongest_evidence: Company cash capacity, credit facilities, growth capex, output/cargo/throughput, fleet OEC, backlog, and EBITDA/DCF proxies are visible.
missing_documents: Project source/use, customer/offtake billing, debt waterfalls, restricted accounts, project EBITDA/DCF contribution, and IRR/NPV/payback.
next_extraction: Create an energy/infrastructure named-project registry for Cheniere trains and Energy Transfer/Nederland/Lone Star capacity rows.
writing_safe_claim: Capital-intensive annual reports show where physical buildout is happening and which companies have cash/facility capacity around it.
do_not_claim_yet: Company EBITDA plus capex proves named-project cash return.

plain_english_question: When utilities spend capital, how does that become customer bills, collections, and earned return?
why_it_matters: This is the public-document route most likely to expose receipts because regulatory dockets sometimes show cost categories, factors, billing bases, and audits.
strongest_evidence: FPL has a strong public docket/recovery route with category costs, factor support, aggregate SPPCRC revenue, discovery, and audit path.
missing_documents: Actual billed and collected receipts by category/rate class/month, category allocation workpapers, legal-entity booking, source-of-funds allocation, and earned-return support.
next_extraction: Run FPL billing-determinant and receipt proof chase as a standalone receipt lane.
writing_safe_claim: Regulated recovery filings can bridge utility spending to authorized customer recovery mechanisms.
do_not_claim_yet: Aggregate clause revenue proves a named category's collected cash or earned return.

plain_english_question: When a financing platform pays upfront for future commodity delivery, does the delivery and settlement cash justify the investment?
why_it_matters: Streaming gives a cleaner two-sided transaction than many themes: payer cash out, recipient cash in, delivery obligation, and later cash-back mechanics.
strongest_evidence: Wheaton/BHP Antamina shows a 4.300B USD named PMPA cash out/receipt route and delivery/cash-back mechanics.
missing_documents: PMPA-only settlement ledger, BHP use allocation, lender draw/use waterfall, tax/interest allocation, reserve-backed IRR/NPV/payback.
next_extraction: Build Antamina settlement-waterfall-return model request packet and public-source limit memo.
writing_safe_claim: Streaming finance has one of the strongest named transaction bridges in the corpus.
do_not_claim_yet: The combined stream cash flow proves BHP PMPA-only settlement or full investment return.

plain_english_question: Who funds acquisitions and backlog growth, and does it convert to revenue, margin, and cash?
why_it_matters: This lane explains how platforms and operators buy capacity, customers, routes, contracts, and backlog rather than building everything organically.
best_companies_or_cases: Sterling; MasTec; URI/Yak; Core Main; MAI; Frontline; Relation; Atwell
strongest_evidence: Sterling and MasTec show backlog/RPO, revenue, adjusted EBITDA, operating cash, credit capacity, and acquisition/platform signals.
missing_documents: Deal funds-flow, purchase accounting, acquired revenue/margin, backlog aging, cancellation risk, retainage collection, project-owner funding, and post-close cash return.
next_extraction: Run backlog/acquisition conversion table for Sterling, MasTec, and one distributor/rollup case.
writing_safe_claim: Backlog and acquisition lanes show capital being converted into operating scale, but project/deal-level return remains unresolved.
do_not_claim_yet: Backlog equals signed funded revenue, or acquisition consideration proves later cash return.

plain_english_question: When companies refinance or reshape debt, who supplies the new cash and who gets paid off?
why_it_matters: This lane is useful because the money path is often more documentable than operating-growth cases: proceeds, redemption, trustee, paying agent, fees, and coupon relief.
best_companies_or_cases: PBF; Matador; Devon; Liberty Broadband; Verizon
strongest_evidence: PBF and Matador show source/use/refinancing proxies and concrete document families for settlement proof.
missing_documents: Trustee settlement statement, paying-agent transfer, borrowing notice, accrued interest, fees, taxes, liquidity impact, after-tax NPV, and operating cash effect.
next_extraction: Select PBF as the refinancing proof case and chase trustee/paying-agent settlement plus value model.
writing_safe_claim: Refinancing filings can get close to a clean source/use proof stack.
do_not_claim_yet: Debt redemption principal proves full refinancing economics or shareholder value creation.

plain_english_question: How does wealth and institutional money enter private markets, and where does liquidity come from when assets stay private longer?
why_it_matters: This is a major annual-report theme around asset managers, but it needs named transaction proof before it becomes cash evidence.
best_companies_or_cases: Blackstone; KKR; Apollo; Ares; Carlyle/AlpInvest; BlackRock
strongest_evidence: The platform map and destination-lane map show wealth alternatives, secondaries, continuation vehicles, and private-market liquidity as major channels.
missing_documents: Investor subscriptions/redemptions, vehicle allocation, named transaction statement, seller cash receipt, fees, distributions, realization, DPI/TVPI/IRR.
next_extraction: Pick Carlyle/AlpInvest or a semi-liquid credit vehicle as a named liquidity case only after source availability is confirmed.
writing_safe_claim: Wealth alternatives and secondaries are important capital-source channels in the platform story.
do_not_claim_yet: Platform fundraising or AUM proves cash reached a named borrower or seller.

plain_english_question: How does money move through receivables, inventory, supplier credit, and cash conversion in operating companies?
why_it_matters: This is less glamorous but very documentable in annual reports and can show whether growth consumes or releases cash.
best_companies_or_cases: Target; Zebra; MSC Industrial; Global Industrial; Pool; Core Main
strongest_evidence: The 519-company source table identifies receivable, inventory, distribution, and asset-backed candidates but most remain queued.
missing_documents: Receivables aging, inventory turns, borrowing-base/collateral detail, customer concentration, gross margin, working-capital cash flow, and collections.
next_extraction: Run a retail/distribution working-capital extraction batch across Target, Zebra, Pool, MSC, and Global Industrial.
writing_safe_claim: Working-capital lanes are promising because receivable and inventory movement can be measured from annual reports.
do_not_claim_yet: Inventory or receivables balances alone prove cash collection or collateral performance.

plain_english_question: Which themes have evidence that capital became durable operating return instead of only assets, debt, backlog, or output?
why_it_matters: This is the synthesis layer that prevents the project from stopping at money movement; it asks whether the money earned enough cash for the risk.
best_companies_or_cases: URI; Sterling; FPL; Cheniere; Ares borrower set; insurance statutory entities
strongest_evidence: The operating-return frontier already ranks URI, Sterling, FPL, Cheniere, Ares, bank replacement, and insurance statutory lanes by source/use/output/cash/durability evidence.
missing_documents: Lane-specific return models, multi-period durability, disproof tests, debt-service burden, asset-level margin, and legal payback/waterfall evidence.
next_extraction: Use this as the prioritization board after each theme-specific extraction refresh.
writing_safe_claim: The research can compare proof quality across lanes using a repeatable source/use/output/cash/durability ladder.
do_not_claim_yet: Any theme with a high proxy score has full investment return proof.
